title: City of Lake Geneva Wisconsin Meeting records

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Wisconsin Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Lacey Reynolds, City Clerk
City of Lake Geneva
626 Geneva Street
Lake Geneva, WI 53147

Dear Clerk Reynolds:

Pursuant to the Wisconsin Public Records Law, Wis. Stat. §§ 19.31-19.39, I request electronic copies of the following records:

1. Audio recordings of the Piers, Harbors and Lakefront Committee meeting held on September 8, 2026, in the complete, unedited form in which they exist.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Gary Milliette

title: DHS Secretary Mullin's November 2026 Trip to Azerbaijan

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: DHS Secretary Mullin's November 2026 Trip to Azerbaijan
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All records created, sent, received, or maintained by the Office of the Secretary of Homeland Security (including the Secretary, the Chief of Staff, the Executive Secretariat, the Office of Strategy, Policy, and Plans, the Office of International Affairs, and the Office of Public Affairs) concerning the Secretary's November 2026 official travel to the Republic of Azerbaijan, including his meeting with President Ilham Aliyev in Baku on or about November 22, 2026. Specifically:

1. The trip itinerary, schedule, and scheduling or advance packages for the visit.
2. Briefing memoranda, background papers, talking points, and agenda documents prepared for the Secretary's meeting with President Aliyev or any other Azerbaijani officials.
3. Readouts, summaries, or after-action reports of the meeting or the trip.
4. Emails, letters, text messages, and other correspondence between DHS personnel and officials of the Government of Azerbaijan (including the Presidential Administration, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the State Border Service, the State Customs Committee, and the Embassy of Azerbaijan in Washington) arranging or discussing the visit.
5. Emails and other correspondence between DHS personnel and the U.S. Department of State or the U.S. Embassy in Baku arranging or discussing the visit.
6. Records sufficient to show the names and titles of the DHS officials and staff who accompanied the Secretary, and the cost of the trip, including aircraft or other transportation, lodging, and security expenses.
7. Records of any gifts exchanged during the visit.

The date range for this request is October 1, 2026 through November 24, 2026.

For the email searches, suggested search terms include: Azerbaijan, Azerbaijani, Baku, Aliyev, TRIPP, "Trump Route", "Zangezur", "South Caucasus".

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, I request that you release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions and identify the specific exemption claimed for each redaction.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am a journalist employed by Reason magazine, and this request is made as part of news-gathering activities and not for commercial use. I also request a waiver of all fees because disclosure is in the public interest: the records concern the operations and activities of the government and are likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of U.S.-Azerbaijan homeland security cooperation.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti
